description: SPEC 9.1 group policies and 9.2 commit authorisation. `default` is the policy of a new group owned by `identities.owner`; `valid` policies parse (canonical JCS); `invalid` ones fail with `error` and `kind`. Each `authorization` case evaluates `facts` (a commit by `committer` with these Adds, Removes, the named `new_policy`, leaves and identities before and after, and `identities_kept`: those with an instance from before the commit that it doesn't remove) against the named policy in force: `result` is `ok` or the error. A case marked `pending` names a SPEC rule the core doesn't implement yet, and must not pass until it does. Rust checks every part; the Python suite checks the policies, and the policy-change cases through check_policy_change, through the bindings.
